findings.ref: reports/implementation/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/T-004.md — "Outputs (confirmation-panel remediation pass, 2026-08-24)" and "Done When Self-Check"; specs/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/tasks.md T-004 "Scope" / "Done When" / "Planned Files"
findings.note: T-004's Done When and Scope both state, verbatim, that `tests/run-all.*` and the staged `test.yml` candidate are "byte-unchanged by this task (no new suite registered -- this task never touches the CI-registration file)", and neither `tests/run-all.*` nor any new suite file appears in Planned Files. The 2026-08-24 confirmation-panel pass nevertheless added `tests/traceability-log-freshness.tests.sh` and `.ps1` and, in the report's own words, "registered in `tests/run-all.{sh,ps1}`"; its Outputs table lists `tests/run-all.sh` and `tests/run-all.ps1` with new SHA-256 values. The report's "Done When Self-Check" was not updated and still asserts PASS on exactly the item this change breaks. This is both an out-of-Planned-Files edit to the shared CI-registration file the task plan deliberately fenced off (tasks.md gives that fence a shared-file-ordering rationale, with T-005 named as the task carrying a direct Blockers edge for it) and a Done-When self-check that no longer matches the shipped diff. The same pass explicitly declined to edit `check-contract.py` because it is "out of every task's own Planned Files" -- the identical reasoning applies to `tests/run-all.*` and was not applied.

findings.ref: specs/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/verification/qg/T-004/regression.log (header) and .../placeholder-scan.log, vs. .../traceability.log and .../focused-tests-{sh,ps1}.log; T-004.contract.json check id "regression" (required: true)
findings.note: The required `regression` check's sole evidence self-dates to "current HEAD (217710a2 + this pass's own uncommitted cycle-3 cross-model panel remediation diff)" -- i.e. the Fifth Pass. The later confirmation-panel pass then changed production code (`_recheck_registry_snapshot`/step 6.5, `_ecma_anchored_pattern`), added the `output-schema-validation-failed-facet-manifest` fixture, and registered two brand-new suites in `tests/run-all.{sh,ps1}`. `traceability.log` and `focused-tests-*.log` were re-captured for that pass (HEAD d392b5e4 + confirmation-panel diff, 201/0), but `regression.log` and `placeholder-scan.log` were not -- they appear in neither that pass's Outputs table nor its "Re-verification" list. Consequence: the full `tests/run-all.{sh,ps1}` baseline enumeration this check rests on was captured before the two new suites existed, so the one pass that edited the CI-registration file is the pass with no run-all evidence at all; likewise the new suite files were never placeholder-scanned. This is the same staleness class the pass claims to have structurally fixed, and the new `traceability-log-freshness` suite guards only `traceability.log`, not `regression.log`.

findings.ref: tests/resolve-project-context-block-check.py — `install_t003_dependencies` (CONTEXT_PROJECTION_SCHEMA_STANDIN / CAPABILITY_SUMMARY_SCHEMA_STANDIN) vs. `GOVERNING_SCHEMA_FILES` in `run_draft7_keyword_coverage_check`; reports/.../T-004.md "Specification Differences" item 2 and "Unresolved Items" (final bullet)
findings.note: Step 12 (`_self_validate_output`) is this task's last defence before a staged artifact reaches a live path, yet no assertion in this suite can fail if the staged Context Projection violates Epic A4's REAL contract. `install_t003_dependencies` unconditionally seeds every fixture repo's `contracts/context-projection.schema.json` and `contracts/capability-summary.schema.json` from the driver's own test-harness stand-ins, and the projection stand-in is deliberately loosened (`projectedComponent: {"additionalProperties": true}`) -- the report acknowledges the loosening and justifies it as "Epic A4's own ... schemas are not yet landed on this branch". That justification is contradicted inside the same report ("Epic A4's own capability-summary.schema.json/context-projection.schema.json are now present at `contracts/` (git root, confirmed directly this pass)") and by the driver itself, whose `GOVERNING_SCHEMA_FILES` reads `ROOT / "contracts/context-projection.schema.json"` and `ROOT / "contracts/capability-summary.schema.json"` for the keyword-coverage check and passes on both. Every step-12 Context Projection self-check exercised by `run_projection_success_case`, `run_t003_case` and `run_t004_case` therefore validates against a self-authored, admittedly-weaker copy, not the governing contract the production code discovers at runtime. (The Capability Summary stand-in is planted but reached by no fixture at all, so the Lite-track half of step 12 is entirely unexercised.)

findings.ref: requirements.md REQ-004 ("A `dsl-warn-on-matched-capability` id therefore never appears with **only** `severity: "warn"` entries and no `severity: "block"` summary entry"); resolve-project-context.py `main()` steps 7-8 abort handlers + `_write_evidence`; tests/resolve-project-context-block-check.py case `evaluate-predicate-failure-after-warn`
findings.note: On the three steps-7/8 abort paths (`registry-validation-failed`, `dependency-subprocess-failed`, `dependency-output-malformed`) `main()` forwards the already-collected `warn_diagnostics` into `_block(...)`. The resulting `diagnostics[]` carries one or more `dsl-warn-on-matched-capability` entries with `severity: "warn"` and a single `severity: "block"` entry under a DIFFERENT id -- exactly the shape REQ-004 says never occurs, because step 9's summary entry is never reached. The in-code comment defending this behaviour answers a different REQ-004 sentence ("no other id ever carries severity: warn at all"), not the one it breaks. The violating shape is then locked in as expected output by the `evaluate-predicate-failure-after-warn` fixture, whose expected `diagnostics` is `sorted([warn entry(dsl-warn-on-matched-capability)] + [block entry(dependency-subprocess-failed)])`, so no assertion in this suite can ever surface the drift. `diagnostics[]` cardinality is this task's declared REQ-004 "Resolver Evidence assembly logic in full" scope by the report's own ownership argument ("T-003 authored WHEN the WARN check fires, not WHAT diagnostics[] contains"). Either the summary entry must also be emitted on those abort paths, or REQ-004's sentence needs a recorded reconciliation; neither exists.

findings.ref: specs/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/verification/T-004.contract.json ("comment", FIFTH PASS ADDENDUM: "GREEN: 184 passed / 0 failed") vs. verification/qg/T-004/focused-tests-{sh,ps1}.log ("RESULT: 201 passed, 0 failed"); reports/.../T-004.md "Done When Self-Check" ("this task's own four new fixtures")
findings.note: Narrative counts in the contract comment and in the Done When Self-Check are one remediation pass behind the evidence they cite: the contract states 184/0 against a cited log that now reads 201/0, and the self-check still says "four new fixtures" while `run_t004_case` runs nine. The evidence pointers themselves are current, so this is prose drift rather than a bad pointer -- but it is another instance of the count-vs-live-artifact staleness class this task has repeatedly been asked about, and the new freshness suite covers only `traceability.log`.

findings.ref: resolve-project-context.py `_resolved_gates` (`if gate_id in seen or gate_id not in gates_by_id: continue`)
findings.note: A `capabilities[].gate_ids` entry naming a gate the discovered Registry does not declare in `gates[]` is silently dropped from `resolved_gates[]` rather than Blocking. Design's Data Plan describes the join but fixes no behaviour for a dangling reference, and decision document v2 s19's governing rule is "曖昧な場合は Block"; no fixture exercises a dangling `gate_ids` entry, so a Registry-side referential defect would surface as a quietly under-populated Facet Manifest. Non-blocking on its own (Epic A2's `validate-capability-registry` may already enforce referential integrity), but the assumption is neither stated nor tested here.
